newsitem.title: INDIA: India, U.S. officials discuss wheat specifications.
newsitem.headline: India, U.S. officials discuss wheat specifications.

text.p: A U.S. delegation and Indian government officials on Friday exchanged views on India's wheat import specifications, a U.S. embassy spokesman said.
"The delegation during its meeting with Indian officials tried to understand Indian specifications for wheat imports," the spokesman told Reuters.
"The visiting delegation also explained to India what were American specifications for selling wheat."
Details of the meetings were not available.
Officials of the state-run State Trading Corp said earlier this month the corporation had contracted to import 2.74 million tonnes since December, mostly from Australia, Canada and Argentina.
Indian newspapers quoted Food Ministry officials as saying on Thursday that the United States was upset at not being able to sell any wheat to India so far.
Officials said American wheat was priced about $15-20 per tonne higher compared to wheat of Australian origin.
"This visit was not for negotiating deals," the spokesman added.
An Indian Food Ministry spokeswoman told Reuters the visiting delegation's discussion with government officials was "of a technical nature".

The team which is visiting India includes representatives of the U.S. Department of Agriculture and U.S. Wheat Associates, plus two members of private companies with extensive expertise in contract procedures.
U.S. Wheat Associates is a non-profit association representing wheat farmers and provides technical assistance to consumers.
